problem: End-to-end supervised VLN agents (even with large augmentation such as ScaleVLN and SRDF) memorize R2R-style language and scenes and generalize poorly to new instruction styles and unseen environments (GSA-R2R). Zero-shot LLM agents generalize more stably but lag far behind fine-tuned models (~36% SR gap) because of weak grounding.
motivation: Navigation is compositional (turning, stairs, landmarks, regions, stopping, temporal order), yet monolithic policies learn conflicting behaviours in one network. Splitting navigation into reusable atomic skills executed by specialists, with a VLM handling high-level composition, could combine LLM-style generalization with precise grounded execution.
key_idea: Train five skill-specialist DUET agents on synthetic skill-specific data, and use a training-free VLM router (temporal reordering, subgoal localization, skill selection) to pick one specialist at each step.
insight: The gains come from structural decomposition, not data volume: a single 'Mixed Skills' DUET trained on the union of all skill data matches ScaleVLN on Test-N-Scene (54.26 vs 54.50 SR) while SkillNav gets 56.66 SR and 47.96 SPL. Temporal reordering adds about 2.5 SPL on Test-N-Scene, and a random router is much worse than VLM routers on Test-N-Scene (43.17 vs 47.96 SPL with Qwen, 48.96 with GPT-4o), so routing matters most under distribution shift. Skill-set ablation on R2R val-unseen shows all five skills give the best results (82.59 SR vs at most 80.80 for four). The main remaining bottleneck is visual grounding: the router under-uses Landmark Detection.
method: Skill taxonomy: four NavNuances skills (Direction Adjustment, Vertical Movement, Landmark Detection, Area/Region Identification) plus two new ones (Stop and Pause, Temporal Order Planning); the Temporal skill is used to build the skill-agnostic backbone.
Synthetic skill data: paths sampled from Matterport3D nodes with skill-specific filters, 4-7 steps; GPT-4o writes R2R-like instructions from trajectory images (2,000 temporal, 450 per atomic skill).

Two-stage agent training: Stage 1 fine-tunes DUET on R2R + ScaleVLN (or SRDF) augmentation + Temporal synthetic data; Stage 2 fine-tunes that backbone separately on each skill dataset to get 5 specialists.
Temporal Reordering Module (GPT-4o): rewrites the instruction into an ordered list of explicit subgoals, resolving 'before/until/once'; the list goes only to the router.
Subgoal Localizer (Qwen2.5-VL-7B zero-shot): from the reordered subgoals, visual history and executed subgoals, picks the next subgoal and outputs a reasoning trace.

Skill Router (Qwen2.5-VL-7B): given the original instruction, current subgoal and trace, chooses exactly one skill agent; the chosen DUET specialist takes the original instruction, panorama and topological map and outputs the action.

setting.backbone: DUET skill agents (fine-tuned; CLIP-B/16 + BERT, or InternViT-6B for SRDF variant) with a zero-shot router: GPT-4o (temporal reordering) + Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (localizer and router)
setting.model_size: 5 DUET specialists plus Qwen2.5-VL-7B router and GPT-4o reorder module
setting.training_data: R2R train + ScaleVLN augmentation (~2.89M instructions) or SRDF augmentation (~414k) + GPT-4o synthetic skill data (2,000 temporal + 5x450 atomic instruction-trajectory pairs); router is training-free
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views of navigable neighbours plus online topological map (discrete nav graph)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (candidate neighbour nodes or stop)

results: SkillNav (ScaleVLN-Aug) gets SR/SPL 57/48 on GSA-R2R Test-N-Scene versus 55/43 for ScaleVLN, and 72/61 on Test-N-Basic versus 69/57. On R2R the SRDF-based variant matches SRDF (val-unseen 84 SR / 78 SPL; test 84 / 77), and the ScaleVLN-based variant gains +3.36 SR and +6.54 SPL on val-unseen over ScaleVLN. NavGPT-2 reaches SR 57 on Test-N-Scene, the same SR as SkillNav.
limitations: Router adds heavy inference cost (~50x slower than ScaleVLN, 0.49 inferences/s) and skill training takes ~55.5 h versus ~42 h for SRDF
Router under-uses Landmark Detection and suffers subgoal hallucination and visual-grounding failures; the DUET controllers fail on stacked commands
Evaluated only on discrete-graph simulators (no VLN-CE or real robots); the five-skill library is hand-designed and indoor-specific
